Synthetic control for one treated unit

Source: R/policy_evaluation.R
synctl.Rd

A weighted average of untreated units that tracks the treated unit before the policy, as its counterfactual after; with the placebo test that runs the same method on every untreated unit.

Usage

synctl(data, unit, time, y, treunit, adopt, plac = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

treunit

The treated unit (a value of unit).

adopt

The first treated period.

plac

Run the placebo test (default TRUE).

Value

A list of class rmbl_synth: weights (a named vector over the donors), path (a data frame: time, treated, synthetic, gap), rmspepre, rmsperatio, p_value (NA without the placebo), placrat. plot() draws the two paths and the gap.

Details

The weights solve $$\min_w \sum_{t < T_0} \Big(Y_{1t} - \sum_j w_j Y_{jt}\Big)^2 \quad \textrm{s.t.} \quad w_j \ge 0,\ \sum_j w_j = 1,$$ over the periods before adoption \(T_0\) (accelerated projected gradient onto the simplex; the problem is convex, so the solution is the global one). The effect in each period is the gap \(Y_{1t} - \sum_j w_j Y_{jt}\). For inference, each untreated unit in turn is treated as if it had adopted the policy, with the other untreated units as donors; the ratio of root mean squared gap after to before adoption ranks the real unit among the placebos, and \(p\) is its rank over the number of units (Abadie, Diamond and Hainmueller 2010).

This version matches on the pre-period outcomes only, not on separate predictors.

References

Abadie A, Diamond A, Hainmueller J (2010). Synthetic control methods for comparative case studies. Journal of the American Statistical Association 105(490):493-505. doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.ap08746

Examples

p <- polex()
p1 <- p[is.na(p$refmonth) | p$district == "D01", ]
s <- synctl(p1, "district", "month", "crmrate", treunit = "D01",
                       adopt = 13)
round(s$weights, 3)
#> D04 D08 D12 D16 D20 
#>   0   1   0   0   0 
s$p_value
#> [1] 1
plot(s)
